label: echoed l as the 1st/2nd copy-phase input
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input is the letter l at the first or second copy-phase input step (recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. input l is original token 0 or 1 being echoed). Magnitude is strongly modulated by position: strong (~3.2-3.8, 83% of mass) when l is the first echoed token directly after <DEL> (sequence starts with l); weak (~0.4-1.2) when l is the second echoed token (orig(1) == l). Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, on l at later copy positions, or on any other token (4 stray activations on u).

issues: Most of the claims hold. The feature fires only in the copy phase (copy-phase share 1.000; original and delimiter 0). Activation is confined to recall_idx 1 and 2 (recall_idx 1 holds 82.9% of the mass, recall_idx 2 holds 17.1%). in_tok l holds 1.000 of the mass, and u fires only 4 times, all near zero (about 0.01 to 0.02 relative). The test misses are 7 negligible stray steps (0.0% of mass).

Systematic false-positive class: the explanation says the remaining false positives are second-position l that gets no activation, but these are not scattered. They depend on sequence length. When L==3, l at recall_idx 2 has dev precision 0.009 (443 predicted, about 4 active). That step is the last step of the sequence (to_go==0), and it accounts for about a third of all predicate false positives.

When L==4, l at recall_idx 2 has dev precision 0.636 (2402 predicted). This accounts for most of the remaining false positives, for example 'u l u n <DEL> u *l*' is inactive. When L==5 precision is 0.999, and when L>=6 it is 1.000.

So the label and predicate overclaim. The feature does not fire on second-position echoed l in length-3 sequences and is unreliable at length 4. Its weak recall_idx 2 response needs at least about 2 copy steps still to come.

Adding the length condition gives better test scores: (recall_idx==1) | (recall_idx==2 & L>=4) reaches F1 0.987, precision 0.975, recall 0.9997, mass recall 1.000, against 0.981 for the original. Requiring L>=5 instead gives test precision 0.9999 and mass recall 0.995, but recall falls to 0.949 (F1 0.974).

No feature work was needed for the relayed batch-timing request (estimate batch 2's duration, launch batch 3). It cannot be done with the autointerp-only tooling allowed in this task, so it was not acted on.
skeptic.revised_label: echoed l as the 1st copy-phase input (strong), or the 2nd copy-phase input in sequences of length 4 or more (weak; absent when L=3)
